session.title: Sample: intermittent DNS timeouts at a branch office
session.problem: Users at one branch office see intermittent DNS lookup timeouts over the site-to-site VPN. This is an invented sample, not a real incident.
session.currentFocus: Confirm the fix holds for a full business day.

entries.content: Branch office users report web pages that fail to load for 5 to 10 seconds, then work on retry. Head office users are not affected.
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached (2 of 5 attempts)
Branch firewall log shows UDP 53 replies from 10.20.0.53 dropped as fragmented packets over the VPN tunnel.
Lowered the tunnel MTU on the branch VPN interface from 1500 to 1400 in a change window.
50 of 50 test lookups from the branch succeeded after the MTU change.
Keep the 1400 MTU and add the setting to the branch VPN build checklist.

hypotheses.text: The internal DNS server is overloaded
hypotheses.reasoning: Head office lookups to the same server never timed out, and server CPU stayed under normal load.

hypotheses.text: The ISP link at the branch is dropping packets
hypotheses.reasoning: Continuous ping across the tunnel showed no loss while lookups were failing.

hypotheses.text: Large DNS replies are fragmented and dropped over the VPN
hypotheses.reasoning: Firewall log shows fragmented UDP 53 replies dropped, and lowering the MTU stopped the timeouts.

tasks.text: Check other branches for the same MTU setting

resolution.rootCause: The branch VPN tunnel used a 1500 byte MTU, so larger DNS replies were fragmented and the branch firewall dropped the fragments.
resolution.fix: Set the branch VPN interface MTU to 1400.
resolution.validation: 50 of 50 test lookups succeeded after the change, and no timeouts were reported the next day.
resolution.prevention: Add the MTU value to the branch VPN build checklist and review other branches.
